title: Frozen nine-objective public-opponent gradient feasibility at retained 1M
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: Although a naive 25%-external public-opponent mixture explicitly harmed all four anchors, a normalized minimum-norm direction over public-opponent reward, six existing anchor-seat reward objectives, the second public seat, and Standard10 forward-KL may still provide replicated common descent at both retained 1M lineages. This audit distinguishes objective incompatibility from insufficient training scale; it is not a poker-strength test.
material_change: Add a frozen non-mutating four-opponent-by-two-seat plus Standard10-KL gradient audit. Use 1,024 deterministic sampled hands per opponent-seat group, both independent 1M checkpoints, four modulo folds, exact raw-hand replay, and no weight updates. Admit a bounded multi-objective update only if both full-lineage worst normalized alignments are at least +0.05 with valid KKT and at least 3/4 folds per lineage have strictly positive common descent.
baseline: Prior six-anchor-seat plus Standard10-KL geometry admitted common descent, but its update had inconclusive breadth translation; naive 25% public-opponent training lost -9.9883 bb/100 versus control across all four anchors. Seed1 retained 1M is externally inconclusive at -21.7592 bb/100 fresh20k while seed1 2M is confidently negative.
source: Frozen seed1/seed2 1M integrated checkpoints, three fixed anchor checkpoints, frozen public Slumbot behavior model, and Standard10 source checkpoint.
notes: Preregistered scale interpretation: failure of this geometry gate rejects this particular public-objective intervention at retained 1M, not long-horizon self-play or opponent-league learning. Success admits only a bounded matched multi-seed intervention before geometric scaling.

Exact full alpha_holdem suite passed 327/327. The public reward aggregate conflicts with Standard10 source KL in both lineages, while the deployed decision-weighted reward plus coefficient-one KL direction harms 3/9 seed1 objectives and 2/9 seed2 objectives. The normalized nine-objective minimum-norm direction remains strictly positive in every fold.

result.summary: Frozen four-opponent-by-two-seat plus Standard10-KL audit completed on both independent retained 1M lineages: 16,384 deterministic internal hands and 39,405 hero decisions. Full-cohort worst normalized common-descent alignments were +0.17714 seed1 and +0.22619 seed2; all four folds in both lineages were strictly positive. Every raw-hand, legal-action, matched-deck, checkpoint, source, opponent, and artifact-integrity gate passed.
result.conclusion: The naive 25%-public mixture remains rejected, but the public reward signal itself is not geometrically incompatible with broad learned-policy improvement. Its full-cohort gradient conflicts with Standard10 preservation in both lineages (cosines -0.5125 and -0.2816), explaining why coefficient summation can drift; normalized nine-objective MGDA resolves that conflict with comfortable replicated margins. This is mechanism evidence only, not external-strength evidence, and does not justify large-scale training without a bounded translation check.
result.next_step: Implement the smallest matched, multi-seed offline update using these exact frozen cohorts: compare the existing seven-objective direction against the nine-objective direction at matched parameter KL/dose, then evaluate untouched three-anchor/two-seat breadth plus public-opponent performance and Standard10 policy preservation. Scale only if translation is broad and replicated; otherwise preserve the retained 1M control and pivot to a different long-horizon learning mechanism.
